subject: Kickoff: Enterprise access controls & SSO/SCIM handoff for MidwestBank
messages:
From: Jill Turner <jill.turner@midwestbank.com>
To: avery_johnson@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Redwood onboarding – SSO/SCIM kickoff & access control scope

Hi Avery,

Thanks again for the demo last week. We’re ready to start the formal onboarding for enterprise access controls (SSO via SAML, SCIM user sync, IP allowlists, and a small set of service accounts).

High level ask: we want a single plan that covers the SSO connection, SCIM attribute mapping (name, email, employeeID, groups), and a short IP allowlist window for our integration tests before we open to production. We also need guidance for service account creation and audit logging expectations (SOC2 space).

Can we schedule a 45-min kickoff this week? Prefer Wed or Thu morning CST. I’ve attached our initial SCIM mapping (midwestbank_scim_mapping_v1.csv) and a short network diagram.

Thanks,
Jill Turner
Director, Identity & Access Management
MidwestBank

Attachments: midwestbank_scim_mapping_v1.csv (CSV stub), network-diagram.png (image stub)

From: avery_johnson <avery_johnson@redwood.ai>
To: Jill Turner <jill.turner@midwestbank.com>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 10:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Redwood onboarding – SSO/SCIM kickoff & access control scope

Hi Jill —

Appreciate the notes and the mapping file. Wed 11/1 09:00 CST works for our team (45 min). I’ve looped in Laura (Customer Success lead) to run the implementation plan and Dev (infra lead) for service-account/IP details.

Quick answers up front:
- SSO (SAML): we’ll do a test IdP metadata exchange, then a staging cert rotation for validation.
- SCIM: we’ll validate the CSV mapping then create a scoped SCIM service account with write-only provisioning permissions.
- IP allowlist: we can provide a short test window (48–72 hours) and a static egress list for production.

Laura, Dev — can you prepare the onboarding checklist and confirm who will own the service account and audit log collection?

Avery Johnson
Senior Customer Success Manager
Redwood Inference

Thanks — looping in the plan below so everyone has a single source of truth before the call. I’ll run the kickoff and own the implementation checklist. Dev, can you own the service account provisioning and the IP allowlist guidance?

Proposed onboarding runway (high level):
1) Pre-kickoff (this week) — confirm SCIM attribute mapping, collect Okta/IdP metadata, share staging endpoints.
2) Week 1 — SSO test connection (SAML metadata exchange), validate SSO attributes (email/name), smoke test login.
3) Week 2 — SCIM sync in staging (limited set of users), confirm group mappings and deprovision behavior.
4) Week 3 — IP allowlist window + performance verification, enable audit log forwarding to customer SIEM (if requested).
5) Go-live — increase SCIM scope and finalize production IP list; service account rotated to production credentials.

Action items assigned:
- laura_bennett: kickoff agenda, runbooks, go/no-go checklist, weekly status updates to Jill/Carlos
- dev_patel: create SCIM service account (scoped), produce IP egress list and recommend firewall rule format, confirm log retention path for audit events
- avery_johnson: executive point of contact, coordinate DRI escalation and procurement questions

Attachments: redwood-sso-onboarding-checklist.pdf (template)

Thanks,
Laura Bennett
Customer Success Lead
Redwood Inference

Hi all — follow-ups from our prep: 

- SCIM mapping: confirmed we support employeeID -> externalId and nested groups are preserved during group sync (we’ll document limitations if group depth > 3).
- Service account example (least-privilege JSON): I’ve pasted a minimal example in the shared Drive doc (see link). We will create a scoped 'scim-provisioner-midwest-<env>' account in staging with write:Users, read:Groups.
- IP allowlist window: Tues 2026-12-07 02:00–14:00 CST is fine; we will provide the egress IPs 48 hours prior. For production we recommend a CIDR list and an expiration process for temporary entries.
- Audit logs: we can forward provisioning events to a customer S3 bucket or push to the SIEM via syslog/HTTPS — Laura, please confirm which method Midwest prefers.

Next steps before kickoff:
1) Laura to share the final agenda and invite (Avery)
2) Midwest to confirm the staging IdP metadata and updated mapping CSV (Carlos)
3) Dev to drop the sample JSON for the SCIM service account and the provisional egress IP list into the Drive folder

I’ll own the service-account creation and will mark the resource as ready in the ticket once done.

Thanks,
Dev Patel
Platform Reliability Engineer
Redwood Inference
